agent.problem: The blank asks for the exact wording "sons," but the earlier cards do not connect the creation's waiting to believers as God's sons. Mentioning that believers are God's children and that creation is waiting does not give the baker enough basis to reason out what the creation is waiting for, so this becomes a guess at wording.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The treatment of Romans 8:20 omits an important part of the verse: creation was subjected not only apart from its own will, but because of the One who subjected it. Cards 5 and 6 establish the futility and negate creation's own will, but no card supplies the positive agent, leaving the account of the subjection incomplete.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

agent.problem: This is a who question, but the wrong answers "Those who never struggle" and "Those who work the hardest" are invented general descriptions rather than real details from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

human.problem: The opening card states facts from Romans 1:1, 1:7 and Romans 8:16-17, and it sets up 8:18. Its "verses" field cites only Romans 8:16-17. The rule says a story card cites from the first verse it uses to the last, which here would run from Romans 1:1 to Romans 8:18. That range makes no sense. The Romans 1 references also appear only inline in the text.
human.question: How should an opening card cite context from outside the passage that comes from more than one place (Romans 1:1, 7 and Romans 8:16-17)? Should the "verses" field hold only the passage verses it sets up, only the outside verses, or something else, with any other references inline?
